source_review.critical_finding: The fixture assigns test_owned=true to a Source ID obtained from a Save UI link, but does not prove that Save created that row. It uses fixed public example.com and IANA URLs. The landing contract exposes reused_existing and new_version_of, and Scrape explicitly says a repeat save keeps the same page as one Source. A returned ID can therefore name a pre-existing organization Source. The cleanup path would soft-delete that exact ID from the organization even though the fixture did not create it. Exact ID matching in cleanup proves row identity, not ownership.

If link discovery or tab navigation fails after landing, fixture.sources remains empty for that row. The catch records only a stage and requires later exact-ID review, but the report contains no ID to review. No safe exact-owned cleanup is then possible from its evidence alone.

source_review.oracle_limit: D65 checks B's title after A network settlement and two animation frames. The assertion can succeed before a late A response has completed its JavaScript continuation and React commit; it does not itself prove B remains selected after all A handling. This is a quality risk to fix before claiming the race is guarded.
source_review.safe_next_step: Use unique, run-specific page identities and establish an absent pre-save baseline for both in the selected organization, then prove the landing returned new rows and durably record each exact ID at the earliest successful boundary. Restrict cleanup to IDs with that provenance. Strengthen D65 to observe a settled UI after A's full handling, including the late-failure path. Re-review source before browser admission.
